headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Devin’s broad shell/git/network and Firecrawl’s API/MCP scraping can create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action paths by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin can use MCP, browsers, and shared integrations, so it may ingest Firecrawl outputs through files or API-fed content; Firecrawl exposes scrape/agent endpoints and MCP-compatible client support, making instruction-like web content plausible. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so injection risk is real though not proven by direct interaction evidence.
conditions: IF Devin reads Firecrawl-sourced HTML/markdown into an agent prompt without provenance filtering, injection is possible.
IF Firecrawl returns attacker-controlled web content that Devin treats as instructions, the pathway activates.
mitigations: Disable automatic prompt ingestion from scraped content.
Add a provenance tag to all Firecrawl outputs before Devin consumes them.
Restrict Devin to read-only review of Firecrawl results.
Use a fixed allowlist of fields from Firecrawl responses.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping middleware.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin handles source code, chat, docs, and integration tokens in a cloud workspace with broad egress; Firecrawl touches web content, structured data, screenshots, and API keys. If Devin forwards Firecrawl outputs or its own workspace data into external APIs, sensitive material can leak across the pair even without a shared filesystem.
conditions: IF Devin is given Firecrawl outputs containing secrets or internal docs, those contents can leave the workspace via broad egress.
IF Firecrawl is used on pages containing credentials or screenshots with sensitive data, Devin may retain or re-export them in downstream artifacts.
mitigations: Limit Devin to non-sensitive test data.
Redact secrets before passing Firecrawl outputs onward.
Turn off unnecessary outbound integrations for the session.
Review exported artifacts before sharing externally.
requires-engineering: enforce data-class-based egress controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin has unrestricted cloud-workspace shell, filesystem write, and git mutation; Firecrawl is an API client/CLI with MCP-compatible support and broad network egress. Their overlapping write-and-network capabilities can conflict on shared repos or API-backed resources, and no locking or coordination primitive is documented here.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or mutable API-backed workspace, concurrent writes can race.
IF Firecrawl and Devin both modify shared git state through integrations, conflicts can corrupt work products.
mitigations: Assign separate repos or branches per agent.
Serialize writes with a simple operator-managed lock file.
Use read-only access for Firecrawl when Devin is editing.
Check git status before and after each agent run.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin is an autonomous planner-executor that can act on browser, shell, and integrations, while Firecrawl is designed for scraping/search and can emit structured outputs that Devin may treat as authoritative. If Devin consumes Firecrawl results without verification, bad web data can cascade into commits, tickets, or messages with irreversible downstream impact.
conditions: IF Devin uses Firecrawl output as ground truth for code, tickets, or messages, errors can propagate.
IF Firecrawl returns stale or adversarial web data and Devin acts on it, downstream actions may be wrong.
mitigations: Require human review before Devin acts on Firecrawl-derived facts.
Cross-check Firecrawl results against a second source.
Restrict Devin from sending emails or writes based solely on scraped data.
Mark Firecrawl outputs as untrusted in the workflow.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before action-taking.

E_compliance.rationale: Devin explicitly touches source code, issue trackers, team chat, and docs, and requests Slack/Linear/Jira/Notion write scopes; Firecrawl touches web content, screenshots, and API keys. That creates a plausible compliance mismatch around retention, residency, and subject-rights handling for scraped or workspace data, though no specific regime is documented in either profile.
conditions: IF EU PII or regulated data is scraped by Firecrawl and then written by Devin into third-party SaaS tools, residency/retention obligations may be violated.
IF either agent retains screenshots or chat/docs longer than policy allows, deletion/export requests may fail.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the shared workflow.
Minimize retention in Slack/Linear/Jira/Notion.
Document which data classes each agent may process.
Purge sensitive artifacts after use.
requires-engineering: map data flows to specific compliance controls and DPAs.
